This release makes the averages in sp_QuickieStore and sp_QueryReproBuilder match Query Store, and it adds a new `@top` parameter to sp_QueryReproBuilder. sp_IndexCleanup no longer disables an index that backs a foreign key, and it judges unused indexes on each database's own usage window. Two patch sets (164 patches, with review fixes) corrected smaller problems in nine procedures and made sp_QuickieStore, sp_QueryReproBuilder and sp_HealthParser faster.
- sp_HumanEvents: the name of a one-shot session now

- On SQL Server 2022 and later, the procedure removes PSP parent queries after their variants. It skips a parent while its variants are still in Query Store. (#883, #884)
- New `@compact_tables`. After the removal, it compacts each index on Query Store's internal tables with `DBCC INDEXDEFRAG`, and it reports each size before and after. It also runs on a READ_ONLY Query Store, where it skips the removal. (#885, #886)
- sp_QuickieCache: `@find_duplicate_plans` returns one row for each query hash in each data

- The summary distinguishes "no waits" from "wait stats capture is off" instead of silently dropping the column. Only 1 of those 11 databases had capture on, and the silent omission fooled the harness that found the rest of this list.

Automatically compiled Install-All from the latest dev push. Not a release: main's tagged releases remain the supported builds.

## Fixed

- Stop all stops every service that is running, including one that is turned off in Settings → Services but was started from its own row. Before, those kept running while Stop all said it was done. If one service fails to stop, the others still stop.
- Start all with every installed service turned off in Settings → Services says so, instead of reporting success with nothing started.
- Share online works for WordPress sites. Before, the public address redirected in a loop. While a WordPress sit

## New

- Polls: a slim panel on the side of the window where you can vote on what we build next, thumbs up or down. Votes are anonymous, one per install. Click its arrow to fold it away. It only shows while there's something to vote on.

- LAN port for a site: other devices on your network (phones, tablets, a colleague's PC) can open a site at `http://<your PC's IP>:<port>`, with no hosts-file edits or certificate. Your `.test` HTTPS address stays as it is. Works with nginx and Apache, needs LAN access on

- Databases → MySQL / MariaDB: if your root account has a password, you can enter it there so EnvKit's database tools can connect.
- MySQL and MariaDB: starting the server stops an earlier EnvKit server that still holds the data files, without killing it. If it doesn't stop, the message gives its PID.
- PostgreSQL: if another user's socket lock blocks the start, the message says who holds it and how to clear it.

- Dropping a MySQL or MariaDB database that another connection has locked now fails in about 8 seconds and says what is holding it, instead of hanging until the client times out.
- PostgreSQL recovering after an unclean shutdown on a slow machine no longer shows as failed to start.
- Databases: the client list still loads when Windows blocks `reg.exe` or `where.exe`.
- MariaDB "Failed to setup SSL" names the `ssl_*` file in my.ini and what is wrong with it.

- A site that fails to create leaves nothing behind: its new folder and new database are removed, so Retry starts clean.
- Databases → Users: create MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL users, set passwords and choose which databases they can use (#180).
- Stopping MySQL/MariaDB is now a clean shutdown instead of a kill, so the next start doesn't run crash recovery. A server that doesn't stop within 20 seconds is still ended.
- Import from XAMPP, Laragon or WampServer installs a database server only if the source

- Windows: folders you add to PATH by hand under EnvKit's data folder (for example `services\mysql\…\bin`) are no longer removed when EnvKit starts (#178).
- Dropping a MySQL/MariaDB database that fails with "can't rmdir … errno 41" now tells you which folder and files are left so you can move them out.
- Databases → Import (PostgreSQL): a dump made by a newer pg_dump (`\restrict` lines) imports into an older server, and a pg_dump custom-format archive saved as `.sql` is restored with pg_restore.

## New

- FrankenPHP worker mode per site (Site → Run → Worker mode). With FrankenPHP as the web server, a site can keep PHP loaded in memory between requests. Laravel runs through Octane's FrankenPHP worker, so it also works on Windows. A worker that fails at boot is taken out and the site keeps serving the normal way; the error shows on the site.

## Fixed

- Python: `python main.py` can import modules that sit next to the script again on Windows (#177). Existing Python installs get the fix the next t

## Fixed

- Windows: nginx no longer shows Failed with "nothing is listening on port 80" while your sites load. On some PCs Windows briefly leaves the port out of its connection list; EnvKit now checks the port itself before calling it not listening, and never restarts nginx over it.
- Site → Share online and Octane: the trusted-proxies line EnvKit adds to a Laravel app now trusts only your own machine (127.0.0.1 / ::1) instead of every address, so it's safe if the app is committed and deployed (#176). An

- Safety: a database folder or certificate authority that can't be read is never replaced or deleted. A PostgreSQL data folder that isn't a cluster is moved aside instead of deleted, and the services list on disk is never rewritten after a failed read.

- Windows: on a busy machine (many open connections), nginx, Apache or a database could show as Failed with "running but nothing is listening on port 80" while the sites still loaded. EnvKit's port check could not read Windows' connection list when it was large; it now reads it in full, and a check that fails never marks a working service as failed.
- Databases: the other admin tools and desktop clients (Adminer, HeidiSQL, TablePlus) are in one "Open in" menu next to the main Open button, instead of a row o

* **Monotonic `_version` across restarts** — a durable version floor seeded at start, GTID path floored by commit order; a commit that reaches the binlog late can no longer lose to an earlier write of its key. ([#1478](https://github.com/Altinity/clickhouse-sink-connector/pull/1478), [#1485](https://github.com/Altinity/clickhouse-sink-connector/pull/1485), [#1452](https://github.com/Altinity/clickhouse-sink-connector/pull/1452))
* **`connect.keep.alive` defaults to `false`** — a lost binlog connection r
